title: Body face — Anek Latin against IBM Plex Sans
type_note: A stretch of 'competitive-benchmark', declared rather than hidden. The subject is two typefaces competing for one role, not two companies. The type's structure — comparison on named dimensions, scored, with a verdict — matches exactly, and registering a bespoke type for a one-off comparison would inflate the vocabulary for no gain. If body-face benchmarks recur, revisit.

capture.method: Chrome DevTools MCP. Glyph proportions via canvas TextMetrics at 200px weight 400 (x-height, cap-height, ascender, per-glyph advance). Digit spacing by DOM width comparison of '1111' against '0000' at 64px, with and without font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums. Both families loaded from Google Fonts and confirmed via document.fonts.check before measuring.

sources.what: Anek Latin, variable 100..800, served by Google Fonts. SIL Open Font Licence.
IBM Plex Sans, weights 100..700, served by Google Fonts. SIL Open Font Licence.

decision_note: The recommendation in this artifact (IBM Plex Sans) was NOT the decision taken. Raquel chose Anek Latin on 2026-08-27, on the grounds that brand.md §6's 'Not IBM' position outranks a metric on a question brand.md owns. Recorded here rather than rewritten so the benchmark keeps saying what it measured — an artifact edited to agree with the decision it informed is worth nothing as evidence.
provenance_note: sha256 is null for both sources: Google Fonts serves a different woff2 subset per user-agent, so a hash would record this session's slice rather than the family. The measurements, not the binaries, are the evidence, and the method is stated so they can be re-taken.
